Paillieux & Boiss }} '''''Salpichroa origanifolia''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Solanaceae|nightshade family]] known by the common names '''lily of the valley vine''',{{Cite web |url=https://plants.usda.gov/home/plantProfile?symbol=SAOR4 |title="Salpichroa origanifolia". USDA Plants Profil |access-date=11 October 2021 |archive-date=11 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011122223/https://plants.usda.gov/home/plantProfile?symbol=SAOR4 |url-status=live }} '''pampas lily-of-the-valley''' or '''cock's-eggs'''.{{BSBI 2007|access-date=17 October 2014 }} ==Distribution and habitat== This species is native to South America (Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay) and is naturalised in Africa (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia), [[Australasia]], Europe (United Kingdom, Italy, Spain, France, Portugal), and North America (United States, Mexico).{{Cite web |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=102338 |title=Germplasm Resources Information Network (GRIN). Agricultural Research Service (ARS), United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). |access-date=11 October 2021 |archive-date=11 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011122221/https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=102338 |url-status=live }} This plant is present in grasslands, roadsides and in neglected areas and may occasionally occur in gardens, at an elevation up to {{convert|100|m}} above sea level. ==Description== [[File: Solanaceae - Salpichroa origanifolia-002.JPG|thumb|240px|left|Fruits]] ''Salpichroa origanifolia'' can reach a stem length of about {{cvt|2-3|m}}. This perennial, rhizomatous, decumbent to climbing, hairy vine has a trailing, highly branched, four-cornered zig-zagging stems. Leaves are glabrous, widely elliptic to ovate or also rounded and can reach a length of about {{cvt|10|-|35|mm}}, with a petiole of about {{cvt|5|-|10|mm}}. The flowers are rather small, {{cvt|1|-|1.5|cm}} long and are born from the axils of the leaves. The calyx lobes reach {{cvt|2|-|3|mm}}. Corolla is bell-shaped or urn-shaped, white or greenish. Anthers reach {{cvt|1.5|-|2|mm}}. Fruits can reach {{cvt|10|-|15|mm}}. They are ovoid berries, ill-smelling and turn white or pale yellow when ripe.[https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?7625,7680,7681 Jepson Flora Project: Jepson Interchange] ==Biology== This invasive vine commonly spreads via seeds and fragments of roots. Seeds germinate from early Spring to late Summer. Flowering occurs at any time but especially in Summer and bears fruits in Autumn. ==Human culture== ''Lily of the valley vine'' is commonly grown as an [[ornamental plant]] in some countries. In others, it is considered an invasive weed. In [[Tasmania]], it is regarded as a toxic weed and its sale and distribution are illegal.{{cite web |title=Pampas Lily-of-the-Valley |website=[[Department of Primary Industries, Water and Environment (Tasmania)|Department of Primary Industries, Parks, Water and Environment]], [[Tasmanian Government|Tasmania]] |date=4 December 2020 |url=http://dpipwe.tas.gov.au/invasive-species/weeds/weeds-index/declared-weeds-index/pampas-lily-of-the-valley |access-date=4 December 2020 |archive-date=2 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202052531/https://dpipwe.tas.gov.au/invasive-species/weeds/weeds-index/declared-weeds-index/pampas-lily-of-the-valley |url-status=live }} ==Gallery== File: Salpichroa origanifolia kz04.jpg|Plant in flower File: Salpichroa origanifolia, fruit.jpg|Ripe fruit File: Salpichroa origanifolia kz03.jpg|Leaves ==References== {{Wikicommons}} {{Wikispecies}} {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q2716586}} [[Category:Solanoideae]] [[Category:Plants described in 1794]] [[Category:Taxa named by Henri Ernest Baillon]] [[Category:Taxa named by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] {{Solanales-stub}}
